_note: Ground truth for tools/rea-bench/targets.c, written before any model saw the binaries. Each task names a function in the stripped binary by its address-independent description; the harness gives the model the decompiled pseudocode (Ghidra via REA) and the question. Scoring: 'exact' = answer must contain the string (case-insensitive, whitespace-insensitive); 'any' = at least one of the strings.

tasks.question: Which well-known hash algorithm is this function based on? Name it.
The function ends with a constant XOR. Give the constant in hex.
This is a repeating-key XOR. Recover the key as an ASCII string.
What 4-byte magic value must the header start with? Give it in hex or as the ASCII it spells.
What is the highest version number accepted?
Which input string makes this function return 1?
This is a linear congruential generator. Give the multiplier and the number of rounds.
The checksum skips bytes with one specific value. Which value (hex or the ASCII character)?
What text format does this parse, and which key does it count?
Which encoding uses this 32-character alphabet? Give the alphabet string or the encoding name.
